why: The other three rulers only ask questions that have an answer, so they can only measure the failure of missing it. They are blind to the opposite failure: returning a confident-looking result when the repository contains no answer at all. Every question here is about a subject neither this repository nor the cold ruler's repository implements, so the only correct reply is no results. A retrieval that answers these is not being helpful, it is guessing, and an agent cannot tell the guess from the real thing.
caveat: Absence cannot be proved by asking, so it is established another way: each question carries the `subject` vocabulary that makes it the question it is, and tests/test_absent_queries.py asserts that none of those words reaches a single unit of the index being graded. Every word here was passed through that check against both repositories rather than chosen by eye -- an earlier draft named `webhook` and `hostname`, both of which this repository has had all along. The check also cost this ruler its two GPU questions: the source explains the coverage bar using `where are CUDA kernels dispatched`, which put those words in the index and made the question answerable. Documentation and ruler cannot own the same vocabulary.
